ai.title: Free tier agent exemption now requires specific model match
ai.summary: The free-tier small-request exemption for lightweight utility agents now requires both the agent ID and the specific model to match, replacing a simple agent-only check. This prevents arbitrary models from being charged zero credits when a lightweight helper like `file-picker` is running them. The change introduces `FREE_TIER_AGENT_MODELS` and `isFreeAgentModel` to enforce this model-level constraint, while updating documentation for daily session limits in the GPT-6.1 Sol promotion to clarify counting behavior.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`, `FREE_TIER_AGENTS` is replaced by `FREE_TIER_AGENT_MODELS` and a new `isFreeAgentModel` helper is added that uses `matchesAllowedModel` to check the agent and model pair; `freebuff-sol-promo.ts` updates the JSDoc for `FREEBUFF_DAILY_SESSION_LIMITS` to explicitly exclude failed starts and fully refunded hours from the session count.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show if any legacy client bundles that rely on the old agent-only exemption will now start incurring minor credit charges for small requests.

eli5.text: The free-tier rule for small, automatic tasks (like quickly finding files) now checks both the task's name and the specific AI model doing the work. Previously, any model could perform these tiny tasks for free as long as the task had the right name; now, the model must also be on an approved list for that specific task. This change affects developers using the free tier who sometimes connect their own AI subscriptions; they will no longer see unexpected small charges when the assistant runs these quick helper tasks, provided the task uses an approved model. For most users, this is invisible maintenance that tightens billing accuracy; no action is needed, and existing sessions do not lose access.
